standard_prerequisites.name: The statement for a single point: a morphism from a reduced scheme into one point of a locally Noetherian scheme, with image exactly that point, factors through the inclusion of the point, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the singleton case on which the finite case is built.

standard_prerequisites.name: The set of minimal primes of a quotient of a Noetherian ring is finite, and the minimal primes of the image of an injective ring map are contained in the image of the corresponding morphism of spectra, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a finite subset of the given set that contains all points of the image, reducing to the finite case.

core_obligations: Singleton case: if the given set consists of one point, the claim is the statement for a single point, which applies because the source is reduced and the target is locally Noetherian (proof lines 15624-15626).

Finite case: if the given set is finite, the assumption on specializations among its points makes it a discrete subspace, so the source with its image in a finite discrete space splits into its fibres and the claim follows from the singleton case applied to each of them (proof lines 15626-15630).

Reduction to the finite case: passing to an affine situation, let the image of the coordinate ring map be a subring of the target ring; its minimal primes form a finite set contained in the image of the corresponding morphism of spectra, hence contained in the given set, and because every other point of the image is a specialization of one of these and the given set has no nontrivial specializations, the image is contained in this finite set, so the finite case applies (proof lines 15631-15643).
proof_roadmap: Dispose of the singleton and finite cases (proof lines 15624-15630).

In general, pass to an affine chart and replace the given set by the finite set of minimal primes of the image subring, using the no-specialization hypothesis to see that nothing is lost (proof lines 15631-15643).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a morphism from a reduced scheme into a set of points of a locally Noetherian scheme with no nontrivial specializations among them factors through the disjoint union of those points (statement lines 15616-15622). The counted proof is short and complete: the singleton case is cited, the finite case follows because the induced topology on the set is discrete so the source splits into its fibres, and the general case is reduced to the finite one over an affine chart by replacing the given set with the finite set of minimal primes of the image subring, which is contained in the image because of the minimal prime statement and exhausts the image because everything else is a specialization (proof lines 15624-15643). It is H2: all three reductions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard statements about points and minimal primes.
